meeting_header:
Date: 2025-02-14T16:00:00Z
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jia Chen (Redwood SE), Monica Reyes (Redwood CSM); Laura Martinez (Helios Head of Security), Ben O'Neill (Platform), Akira Sato (Legal), Priya Kapoor (Infra)
summary: Redwood and Helios discussed EU data residency requirements, region pinning, cross-border processing concerns, and KMS/sub-processor disclosures. Helios requested EU-only deployment options, BYOK details, audit log retention, and confirmation that fallbacks wont cross borders without consent. Next step is an infra deep-dive and delivery of docs and config examples.
topics: Data residency and region pinning (EU-only deployments)
Audit logs, retention, and export controls
Fallback behavior and smart routing policies
transcript: [00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Laura Martinez: Laura here from Helios security. Hi Samir, Jia.
[00:12] Ben O'Neill: Ben, infra. Priya is on as well but will chime in later.
[00:20] Samir Patel: Great. We set aside 40 minutes to focus on region pinning and any data residency constraints you have. Jia will cover the technical details.

[00:30] Jia Chen: Hi team. I will lay out how Redwood supports region pinning, EU-only deployments, and what falls under cross-border processing. Quick disclaimer, some terms might be slightly different in the console UI — we call it route pinning and region affinity in the product, but same idea.
[00:45] Priya Kapoor: Important for us is that no customer data leaves the EU for processing or for caching without explicit approval. Also concerned about third-party logging and backups.

[00:55] Jia Chen: Understood. For hosted customers we have dedicated EU regions. You can opt to pin requests to eu-west-1 like behavior — basically a configurable region constraint. For Dedicated or Private we can guarantee the compute is in your VPC/region. There is also an option for 'EU only' routing at the account level.
[01:20] Ben O'Neill: What about fallbacks? If EU capacity is saturated, will requests go to US automatically? That's a showstopper for us.

[01:28] Jia Chen: By default we have smart routing that can failover for availability, but for customers requiring strict residency we enforce region hard-pinning which disables cross-region failover. There is also a canary policy so you can test a small percentage to fallbacks but you have to opt in.
[01:48] Laura Martinez: Ok we need something auditable in the policy. Can you show where that's configured?

[01:54] Jia Chen: Yes, we'll send the Terraform examples. In the console it's a region pin flag; in Dedicated it's part of the capacity pool config. Note one caveat: some auxiliary services like telemetry ingestion or analytics pipelines may be processed in other regions unless you choose the EU-only observability addon. We'll include the sub-processor list.
[02:20] Akira Sato: Legal wants the sub-processor list and their processing regions. We also need contractual clauses for data transfers. Do you support SCCs / EU standard contractual clauses?
[02:30] Samir Patel: We do provide SCCs and our legal team can add the needed exhibits. I'll coordinate that. We'll also share the most recent sub-processor register.
[02:40] Priya Kapoor: For KMS, we require BYOK and HSM-backed keys. Can we bring our own keys?

[02:47] Jia Chen: Yes, BYOK is supported. For hosted we integrate with major cloud KMS providers and we also support customer-managed keys via an envelope encryption flow. For Dedicated and Private you can connect your KMS over a peered connection and we can route key ops to your HSM. Minor note: some logs still contain metadata about request routing which may go to our central logging unless you enable private logging retention.
[03:15] Ben O'Neill: How about audit logs — retention, tamper evidence, exportability?

[03:22] Jia Chen: Audit logs are stored in append-only storage, retention is configurable. We can ship exports to your S3 bucket in the EU on a schedule or provide streaming via a private log forwarder. There is also an immutable retention mode for compliance purposes.
[03:40] Laura Martinez: Are audit logs encrypted with the same keys or separate?
[03:44] Jia Chen: They are encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys if you enable BYOK for logging. By default we use our platform KMS, but you can enable your key per-tenant.
[04:00] Akira Sato: Cross-border processing: what counts? For example, do your model providers or sub-processors do any inference outside the EU?

[04:10] Samir Patel: Good question. For open model hosting we spin up model replicas in the region you specify. However if you choose to use certain managed components or partner services (for example, a third-party eval service) those may operate outside the EU. We will mark those in the sub-processor register. Also note cached KV entries can be retained in the serving region; we avoid replicating KV state across borders unless configured.
[04:40] Ben O'Neill: We care about embeddings and any pre- or post-processing. Does Redwood ever send payloads to external partners for things like toxicity checks or logs enrichment?
[04:50] Jia Chen: Not by default. There are optional addons that run analytics which could involve third-party services. Those are opt-in and documented. We'll provide a full breakdown.
[05:05] Priya Kapoor: Regarding SSO and RBAC — we use Okta and SCIM. Is SAML/SCIM supported?

[05:12] Monica Reyes: Yes, we support SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. Role-based policies can be scoped by project and route so only selected engineers can deploy or change region pinning. We advise least privilege for production routes.
[05:30] Laura Martinez: Do we get field-level logging redaction? We can't have plain PII in logs.
[05:36] Jia Chen: We provide configurable log redaction rules. The SDKs can mask or hash fields before sending and on the platform we can apply filters to redact sensitive fields server-side as well.
[05:50] Ben O'Neill: About backups — are snapshots geo-redundant? If so, where are they stored?

[05:56] Jia Chen: Snapshots for hosted standard are geo-replicated for DR; for EU-only compliance you can opt into single-region snapshots or Dedicated where backups remain in customer-controlled storage. We'll detail the backup topology in the doc.
[06:15] Laura Martinez: On encryption in transit, do you support mTLS between your control plane and customer VPCs for private?

[06:21] Jia Chen: Yes, we support mTLS and cert pinning for control-plane to data-plane connections in Private and Dedicated setups. For hosted there's TLS v1.2+ and optional mutual TLS for specific integrations.
[06:35] Akira Sato: Can you promise no cross-border processing for EU-only customers in contract?

[06:42] Samir Patel: We can contractually commit to EU-only processing for hosted EU-only and Dedicated EU deployments. There are edge cases — like legal requests or emergency incident response — that we will handle following the contract; we'll map those exceptions clearly in the DPA.
[06:59] Ben O'Neill: Regarding sub-processors, which cloud providers and regions do you use for EU services?

[07:06] Jia Chen: Primarily AWS eu-west-1 and eu-central-1, with options for GCP europe-west and Azure West Europe depending on availability. We'll enumerate endpoints per service region in the register.
[07:22] Priya Kapoor: We need a test plan for an EU-only pilot including traffic shaping and latency numbers. Can you run a benchmark with your dedicated pool?

[07:29] Jia Chen: Yes. We'll propose a pilot: stand up a dedicated EU pool, run our standard perf harness with your payload shape, and provide latency and cost numbers. That will also show any cross-service calls.
[07:44] Laura Martinez: For encryption keys, one ask: can we rotate keys without downtime?

[07:49] Jia Chen: Key rotation is supported for customer-managed keys. We do a rolling rotation for live workloads. For certain HSM-backed flows there may be a short micro-window to re-establish sessions but we avoid full downtime.

[08:05] Samir Patel: Quick note: some of the product names in docs are outdated — you might see Redwood Dedicates or Redwood Privatee. Sorry, our docs team is consolidating names. We'll send the canonical doc links.
[08:18] Akira Sato: Legal will want proof points (SOC2 report, ISO cert) and a contact for data access requests. Can you provide the latest attestation?
[08:25] Samir Patel: Absolutely. I'll attach SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 cert copies. For DSRs/data subject requests we have a documented process and a dedicated point of contact.
[08:36] Ben O'Neill: Any limitations around model caching that could cause data to persist in unexpected places?
[08:41] Jia Chen: We use KV cache to speed up autoregressive workloads. For EU-only we keep KV in-region. Cache TTL is tunable and you can disable persistent cache for sensitive routes.
[09:00] Laura Martinez: About telemetry — do you sample payloads? We need to be sure raw inputs aren't captured in central analytics.
[09:07] Jia Chen: Telemetry sampling is off by default for PII, and you can configure sampling/exclude rules. We also allow forwarding telemetry to your own analytics endpoint in the EU.
[09:20] Priya Kapoor: How are secrets handled in transit between Redwood and our KMS?
[09:25] Jia Chen: We use envelope encryption: we never send plaintext keys to Redwood. Key ops happen in your KMS with signed requests. The platform only stores key metadata and encrypted DEKs.
[09:40] Akira Sato: One more legal nuance: will you sign data processing addendum that specifies controller vs processor roles?
[09:46] Samir Patel: Yes, we provide a DPA that clarifies roles. We'll include SCCs and any export controls in the DPA exhibit where needed.
[09:58] Monica Reyes: To recap, action items: we'll send SOC2/ISO, region pinning examples, KMS checklist, and sub-processor register. Samir will loop legal. Jia will propose pilot timing.

[10:10] Laura Martinez: Sounds good. Couple small clarifications to follow up: 1) confirm no analytics pipeline leaves EU, 2) provide exact console path for enabling region pin, 3) sample Terraform snippet.
[10:25] Samir Patel: We'll do that. Monica will send calendar invites for the infra deep-dive. Thank you all.
[10:32] Ben O'Neill: Thanks, bye.
[10:35] Akira Sato: Thanks everyone.
[10:37] Jia Chen: Bye.
